newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks end sharply down on selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks end sharply down on selling pressure.

text.p: Dhaka stocks closed sharply lower as selling pressure mounted from investors anticipating further falls. Brokers said this was due to reports that a government inquiry might implicate big market players in alleged manipulation of share prices during a lingering bull-run last year.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange all-share price index closed 86.52 points or 6.97 percent down at 1,153.52 on a turnover of 70.6 million taka. Of 119 traded issues 108 lost and 9.0 gained.

"The investors were trying to escape from a falling market. They are nervous about the news that the government would take action against those responsible for the euphoric hike in share prices during the October-November trading," said broker Shahidullah Shamoyl.
An inquiry committee formed to probe the alleged manipulation is due to finalise its report later this week.
Singer Bangladesh shed 643 taka to 8,643, Bangladesh Lamps lost 430 taka to 4,053 and Amam Sea Food Industries fall 320 taka to 2,891.
